_comment: P2-8 (2026-09-04 launch-audit follow-up). Every SECURITY DEFINER function in the public schema starts life with the default Postgres PUBLIC EXECUTE grant unless someone explicitly REVOKEs it -- that miss is exactly what let expire_abandoned_checkout_attempts() ship directly callable by anon/authenticated on 2026-09-03 (fixed in migration 20260904160000, caught by re-auditing the 2026-09-02 P0-1 sweep's own list a day later, not by any standing CI check). This file is the explicit, reviewed exception list for scripts/security-definer-grant-sweep.mjs: any SECURITY DEFINER function found with a PUBLIC/anon/authenticated EXECUTE grant that is NOT listed here fails the nightly sweep. Two legitimate categories, both harmless by construction rather than by convention -- adding an entry here is a real security review, not a rubber stamp:

categories.rls-helper: Called BY RLS policies themselves (auth.uid()-derived predicates like is_admin(), get_my_student_id(), is_teacher_of(id)) -- Postgres evaluates these as the querying role, so they must stay executable by anon/authenticated or every RLS policy that calls them breaks. None of these accept a caller-supplied identity to impersonate; they only ever resolve the CURRENT auth.uid().
categories.trigger: RETURNS trigger -- Postgres only invokes these via the trigger mechanism on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against the table they're attached to. PostgREST cannot expose a trigger function as a callable RPC regardless of its grants (there is no `/rpc/<name>` route for a trigger-returning function), so an EXECUTE grant on one is inert from an external-caller perspective.
